from: October book, night 20 (We Are the Clay)
p1: Long ago, Isaiah’s people had turned away from the Lord. Isaiah wanted them to come close to Him again. So he said a prayer.
Isaiah prayed, “O Lord, You are our Father. We are the clay, and You are our potter.”
In Isaiah’s day, everyone used clay bowls and jars. A potter made them, shaping soft, wet clay with his hands.
p2: Isaiah prayed, “We all are the work of Your hand.” A potter shapes clay slowly and carefully into something good. The Lord gently shapes us too, as we listen and learn.
You are His work, made with love. Bit by bit, Heavenly Father helps you grow kind and good like Jesus.
old: A long time ago, Heavenly Father’s people were far from home, and their beautiful temple was broken down. They were sad, and they had made many mistakes. A prophet named Isaiah prayed for them. A prophet is someone Heavenly Father teaches, so he can teach everyone else.
Isaiah found soft, gentle words. He said, “Heavenly Father, You are our Father. We are the clay, and You are the potter. We are all the work of Your hands.”

A potter is someone who makes bowls and cups out of soft, squishy clay. Everyone in Isaiah’s town had clay bowls, so they all knew just how a potter works. The clay cannot make itself into a bowl. It sits still in the potter’s hands and lets him shape it, slowly, until it turns into something good.

Isaiah was saying that Heavenly Father works like that potter. He is patient. He is never rough. Even when His people had made mistakes, He did not throw them away — He kept shaping them, kindly, with His own hands. That is why Isaiah used the picture of clay: to remind the sad people that they still belonged to Him. Jesus helps shape us gently too.
You are the work of His hands as well — every finger, every eyelash, every idea in your head. You are not finished yet. And you are loved already, right now, tonight.
